title: Cross-region procurement heuristics & model-velocity probe
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: produce a reproducible playbook linking model availability velocity (how quickly a model can be provisioned or failed over across regions) to procurement heuristics used by enterprise buyers. We will quantify regional latency tolerance bands, define procurement velocity tiers (express, standard, slow), and propose a decision tree that informs: reserved vs hosted choices, preferred fallback model families, and contract SLAs. This work synthesizes competitive signals (model supply volatility), synthetic cohort experiments, and customer interviews to surface operational triggers for sales and SRE teams.

acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published with procurement velocity tiers and decision tree (Confluence + Notion links)
Three cohort experiments completed (consumer/enterprise/finserv) with reproducible scripts and dashboards
Signal hub prototype that emits region-model velocity and suggested fallback variant (prototype webhook or CSV)
Stakeholder review completed with Sales, Legal, and SRE and at least one pilot customer committed to test run
metrics: Primary: mean time to failover (seconds) by region and model family
Primary: P95 latency under production-like load for each cohort
Secondary: per-token cost delta when switching to fallback model
Secondary: customer acceptance threshold captured in pilot feedback
tradeoffs_and_notes: Quantized model fallbacks reduce cost and sometimes provisioning time but can introduce quality regressions; include evals in the roll-forward checklist.
Reserved capacity reduces failover risk but increases committed spend; playbook must show breakeven against outage-cost estimates for buyers.
APAC regions show higher variance in provisioning lead time due to spot capacity variability; recommend warm pools or regional replication for critical customers.
